title: places
aim: Describe cities, neighbourhoods, journeys and city transport.
objectives: Use be/get used to for familiar and new situations
Ask for and confirm information about transport
Describe areas of a city and epic journeys
Present a city and its traditions

grammar.title: so and such
grammar.shortAr: so + صفة/ظرف للتأكيد، و such + a/an + صفة + اسم مفرد، أو such + جمع/اسم لا معدود. مع that تُبيّن النتيجة: It was so cold that we needed coats.
points: Use so + adjective/adverb for emphasis: so beautiful, so brilliantly.
Use so + adjective/adverb + that for a result: It was so cold that we needed coats.
Use such + a/an (+ adjective) + singular noun, or such + plural/uncountable noun: such friendly people.
table: That part of the city is so beautiful!
The restaurant was so busy that we couldn’t get a table.
It was such a boring job that she decided to change companies.
exceptions: In informal speech that can be omitted: I was so tired (that) I fell asleep.

vocab.example: There are so many diverse neighbourhoods in Toronto.
It’s a very wealthy neighbourhood.
It has these huge tree-lined avenues.
The architecture is really interesting and unique.
There are no high-rise buildings there.
The district is covered with colourful murals and street art.
It has such lively nightlife, too.

listening.summary: Three people describe their favourite neighbourhoods: Rosedale, Barranco and Yarraville.
Emphatic so/such sentences about places and food.

video.summary: People name their favourite cities, including Katowice, Rio, Valencia, Lisbon and Paris, and say why.

practice.q: It was ___ cold that we needed coats.
practice.why: so + adjective + that shows the result.

grammar.title: be/get used to
grammar.shortAr: be used to + اسم/ing يعني معتاد على شيء، و get used to يعني أصبح معتاداً. أمّا used to + مصدر فهي عادة في الماضي.
points: be used to + noun/-ing = accustomed to something that is normal for you: I’m used to flying.
get used to + noun/-ing = become accustomed; it is no longer strange: I soon got used to it.
used to + infinitive describes a past habit or state, not the same as be/get used to.
table: I’m a pilot, so I’m used to flying.
At first I didn’t like the food, but I soon got used to it.
We never got used to the pollution in the city.
We used to live on a boat. Now we live in a house.
exceptions: After be/get used to use -ing, not the infinitive: I’m used to working at weekends.

vocab.example: I take just one small suitcase and nothing else.
We’ll break the journey halfway and go for lunch.
I got tired of living out of a suitcase.
I was alone, so I had to think on my feet.
I worried I would get into hot water with the airport staff.
You just need to weather the storm. Things will improve.
They drive the crew to the launchpad.

reading.summary: Article about epic journeys and the challenges travellers face far from home.

listening.summary: Examples: I’m used to travelling alone; I got used to the cold.

practice.why: be used to is followed by -ing.

practice.q: At first it was strange, but I soon got used to ___.
We ___ live on a boat, but now we live in a house.
practice.why: used to + infinitive describes a past habit.

lessons.title: City transport

grammar.title: How to ask for and confirm information
grammar.shortAr: للتأكيد: So what you’re saying is... / If I’ve got this right... / So let me just check. ولطلب الإعادة: Can you just say that last bit again?/I didn’t catch what you said about...
points: Confirm with So you’re saying…, In other words… or If I’ve understood correctly, what you’re saying is…
Ask for repetition with Can you just say that last bit again? or Could you just go through those options again?
Say I didn’t catch/understand what you said about… to ask about a specific point.
table: So what you mean is we have to buy our tickets over there.
So let me just check I’ve got this right.
Could you just go through those options again please?
I didn’t catch what you said about the cost.
exceptions: Use the right form: If I’ve got this right (not getting); can you just say (not to say).

vocab.example: I’d recommend the Thames Clipper river boats.
The cruises designed for tourists are much more expensive.
The Clipper is part of London’s public transport.
You can just use your travel card.
You tap in and tap out at each end.
You can hop on and hop off at any point.
The boat passes many of London’s famous landmarks.

listening.summary: A conversation about seeing London’s sights by Thames Clipper river boat.
Discussing a proposal for smart roads and fewer cars in the city.

speaking: Roleplay asking for and confirming information about city transport.
writing: Write instructions for how to get somewhere.

practice.q: Sorry, can you just ___ that last bit again?
practice.why: can you just + infinitive without to.

practice.q: So let me just ___ I’ve got this right.
If I’ve understood ___, we’re too late.

lessons.title: A city of tomorrow
goals: Present a city and its culture

grammar.title: Presenting a place: signposting language
grammar.shortAr: عبارات لتنظيم حديثك عن مدينة: I’m going to talk about... / An example of... / So, for example... / Another speciality... / When it comes to...
points: Open with I’m going to talk about my adopted city of Oviedo…
Introduce examples with An example of the culture is… or So, for example, let’s take fabada.
Add and change topic with Another speciality of the region is… and When it comes to music…
table: I’m going to talk about my adopted city of Oviedo.
An example of the culture is Oviedo’s architecture and public art.
Another speciality of the region is rice.
When it comes to music, the region has its own instruments.

vocab.example: Its music, language and food are cultural traditions.
The old town is famous for its medieval buildings.
There are many sculptures in public places.
Another speciality of the region is rice.
Fabada is like a type of stew.
One instrument is similar to a Scottish bagpipe.
There are a growing number of expats in Shenzhen.

listening.summary: A talk about Oviedo: its architecture, public art, food, language and music.

video.summary: Documentary: Reggie in China explores Shenzhen’s growth, innovation and ‘Shenzhen Speed’.

speaking: Talk about what a place is famous for.
Discuss a proposal for a city of tomorrow (MEDIATION).
writing: Write a description of a business idea.

practice.q: ___ example of the culture is its architecture.
practice.why: example starts with a vowel sound.

practice.q: Fabada is a dish made of beans and meat, ___ a stew.
___ it comes to music, the region has its own instruments.
practice.why: When it comes to… changes the topic.
